A1.justification: Both 12-page PDFs describe the same VA-GPT study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both mention supplementary details without including them.

before.justification: v1 reports original VA-GPT evaluations on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MMEval, alongside ablations and qualitative examples in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative examples in Section 4 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same SETS selection procedure, TETG temporal tokens, anomaly-aware classifier, loss, and two-stage training strategy.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same instruction-training data, UCF-Crime and XD-Violence evaluations, MMEval benchmark, and short-, medium-, and long-video examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same eight comparison models. Table 2 retains A-Guardian, while Table 4 retains Video-ChatGPT and LLaMA-VID in the fine-tuning comparison.

E3.justification: The reported QA evaluation procedures, accuracy metrics, model configurations, training-data counts of 4,077 videos and 7,730 images, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same component and training-stage ablations, fine-tuning comparison, and SETS sampling-rate analysis. The cross-domain evaluation and qualitative cases in Figures 3–4 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for its experiments. Results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and the qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains VA-GPT's total/temporal accuracies of 30.69%/35.00% in-domain and 26.20%/31.02% cross-domain.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), token and mask definitions, and associated mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning VA-GPT, SETS/TETG, anomaly instruction data, and the cross-domain benchmark.

C2.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same interpretations of token filtering, data quality, and generalization, together with the same limitation concerning detection and description of complex scenes.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including PyTorch, four NVIDIA A100 GPUs, AdamW, batch size 64, learning rate 2e-5, cosine decay, and one epoch. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 86 reference entries, and the positioning relative to existing MLLMs and video anomaly detection methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes 'Wilton W.T.Fok' to 'Wilton W.T. Fok' and updates the arXiv version/date label. PDF author metadata changes 'Ruifan Di' to 'Ruidi Fan', matching the existing printed byline. Body wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–5 retain the same visuals, captions, structures, and locations. The page organization and two-column layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes a small author-formatting and metadata correction and updates version/date information. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations remain unchanged, leaving no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
